question: At the canonical top-32 operating point, do the 16 documents select nearly the same slots and overwrite each other -- and if so, is ORACLE-WRITE's 'perfect value write reaches only MT 2.381' an artefact of allocation rather than a property of value-only writing?
variable_under_test: none (pure instrumentation of the canonical EXP-007-top32 configuration; no config or code was changed)
baseline_ref: EXP-007-top32 (QA 2.1766157150268555 / MT 2.5483615398406982), reproduced to all 16 digits in this run

q2_survival_HEADLINE.definition: fraction of the slots document d wrote that NO later document re-selected

q3_slot_mass_bandwidth.convention: layer-average of the mean cartridge-renormalised routing mass on the slot set, untouched Phase-1 cartridge
q3_slot_mass_bandwidth.verdict: 70.4% reproduced exactly (0.70437 MT); 15.2% is the SAME quantity under a different aggregation (this run gives 0.1524 in that aggregation and 0.2037 in the aggregation the 70.4% uses). Once the unwritable frozen sink is excluded the gap disappears: 0.1954 vs 0.2037 at a smaller budget, 0.2373 budget-matched (1.17x).
q3_slot_mass_bandwidth.cross_validation: eval-time absolute mass on the written union reproduces ORACLE-WRITE to 4-5 s.f. (MT 0.08961 vs 0.08956; QA 0.08272 vs 0.08272; cartridge mass MT 0.58787 vs 0.58787)

q4_document_disagreement.note: USE_IDF=0 verified: ranking_info.tfidf == ranking_info.tf bitwise, so the score is purely the per-document access score

command: bash research_loop/results/DIAG-OVERWRITE/launch_diag_overwrite.sh  (canonical AM top-32: USE_IDF=0 SLOT_SELECTION=tfidf GRANULARITY=per_layer TOP_T=32 TARGET_MODE=cartridge_plus_doc KEY_MODE=freeze RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4 RIDGE_SCALE=spectral DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2 AM_EXECUTION_MODE=per_document MAX_QUERIES_PER_HEAD unset(=64) PHASE1_CACHE_PATH=outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/cache_last.pt, RUN_NAME=DIAG-OVERWRITE_top32 WANDB_GROUP=B-OVERWRITE WANDB_DISABLED=0) ; then bash research_loop/results/DIAG-OVERWRITE/launch_slot_mass.sh ; then research_loop/results/DIAG-OVERWRITE/{analyze_overwrite.py,log_wandb.py}. NO source file was edited: all four quantities come from artefacts the stock run already writes (am_doc_*.pt, cache-after-*.pt) plus one standalone forward-pass script. Imports pinned to the frozen snapshot /tmp/amsnap_ovw (git archive HEAD {cartridges,examples} at f5687216; manifest sha256 f0355ea26b754d240551ada0a9db5a2501c82b198fdc5396a5ecbc01a84c6e41, re-verified unchanged after the run); CARTRIDGES_DIR pinned there too; cartridges.__file__ = /tmp/amsnap_ovw/cartridges printed from cwd=/tmp in every job log.
observations: No instrumentation hook was needed: the stock per-document path already saves each document's selected slots (am_doc_*.pt) and a full cache snapshot after each write (cache-after-*.pt, SAVE_AFTER_EACH_DOCUMENT defaults to 1), so the run is the canonical one and reproduced EXP-007-top32 to all 16 printed digits on both splits (QA 2.1766157150268555 / MT 2.5483615398406982). (1) COLLISION: the 16 documents' per-layer top-32 selections have mean pairwise Jaccard 0.713, the per-layer union is 54.4 slots (35-79), so 512 slot-writes per layer land in 54.4 distinct slots = 9.83 writes per slot; 31.4 slots per layer are written by >=8 documents and 18.6 by all 16, and 87.3% of all 18432 slot-writes go into slots touched by >=8 documents. (2) SURVIVAL, the headline: the fraction of a document's slots that no later document re-selects is 4.9% for document 1, 1.0% for document 8, 17.0% for document 15 and 100% for document 16 -- mean 4.7% over documents 1-15. Numerically the values are not fully erased, because the DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2 trust region anchors each solve to the incumbent value: document 1's written values still move by a median 99% of their own magnitude (cos(final, as-written) = 0.517) and the later documents' net change to its slots is 30x larger than the change document 1 itself made; by document 15 the drift is 7% and the cosine 0.965. Each of document 1's slots is re-written by 11.8 later documents on average. (3) BANDWIDTH: this run's own forward pass reproduces ORACLE-WRITE/DIAG-ROUTING to 4-6 s.f. (mass on the union MT 0.08961 vs 0.08956; cartridge mass 0.58787 vs 0.58787) and reproduces SCOUT-KEYS' mass-ranked per-layer top-32 figure exactly (0.70437 vs 0.7044) -- but the 15.2%-vs-70.4% pair mixes two aggregations of the same quantity (in the aggregation the 70.4% uses, the written union carries 0.2037, not 0.152) AND 0.5113 of the 0.7044 is the single FROZEN sink slot 0, which no AM config can write. Restricted to writable slots a mass-ranked per-layer top-32 carries 0.1954, i.e. 0.96x the tf-idf union at a smaller budget; budget-matched (54.4 writable slots) it carries 0.2373 (1.17x) and per-head 0.2598 (1.28x). The 4.6x writable-bandwidth gap is refuted. (4) DISAGREEMENT: the documents' per-layer slot scores have mean Spearman 0.958 across all 120 pairs (min over layers 0.714) and each document's top-32 overlaps a document-INDEPENDENT top-32 (built from the across-document mean score) by 87.4%, so the selector carries very little document-specific information. Caveats: the survival number in (2) is a property of the selection sequence and is exact, but 'overwritten' is not 'erased' -- the trust region keeps a partial trace, which is why the value cosine is 0.52 rather than 0; the eval-time masses in (3) are on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge (the post-write cache was not re-measured here); the Q1/Q2/Q4 numbers are bit-identical to those recomputed from ORACLE-WRITE's independent control run of the same config, which is a same-seed reproduction and confirms plumbing, not seed-robustness.
